question.text: Will a televised debate featuring at least three of Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau air on 26 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if at least one televised debate is broadcast starting on 26 November 2026 (Spanish local time, CET) in which at least three of the following four people take part in person as debaters: Pedro Sánchez (PSOE), Alberto Núñez Feijóo (PP), Santiago Abascal (Vox) and Ada Colau (Frente Amplio). Only these four named individuals count toward the three; a party spokesperson or substitute taking part in place of one of them neither counts toward the three nor disqualifies the programme. A "televised debate" means a programme carried by a Spanish television channel available nationwide, in which the participating candidates appear together in the same studio session and take part in a joint political discussion; appearance only in a separate segment or pre-recorded clip does not count, and the broadcast must begin between 00:00 and 23:59 CET on 26 November 2026. Resolution is based on the record of debates held on 26 November 2026 compiled in the Doble Lectura debates tracker (https://doblelectura.es/guia/debates-electorales-elecciones-generales-2026); if that tracker does not record the relevant programme, the broadcasters' own programming information or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used. If no such programme airs starting on that date, the question resolves NO.
question.fine_print: Broadcasters' labelling is not decisive: a programme that meets the definition above counts whatever it is called, and a programme that does not meet it does not count even if billed as a debate.

research:
Here is what I found. In short: several outlets report that a four-way debate between the leaders is planned for 26 November, but nobody has formally confirmed it yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-15: The Doble Lectura tracker ("Datos a 15 de noviembre") lists item 6 as "Jueves 26 de noviembre: Debate a cuatro con la Academia". Its note says the debate is planned, according to Vozpópuli, with the Academia and RTVE, but has no confirmation from the Academia or the parties and no time. It also notes that Podemos wants to take part. [Doble Lectura](https://doblelectura.es/guia/debates-electorales-elecciones-generales-2026)
- 2026-11-15: The same tracker lists an Atresmedia four-way on Monday 23 November. Feijóo and Abascal have accepted, Frente Amplio backed out, Sánchez has not committed, and it is unclear whether it will happen. RTVE's 8-party spokespeople debate is on 23 November at 22:00. [Doble Lectura](https://doblelectura.es/guia/debates-electorales-elecciones-generales-2026)
- Politicheck was last updated on 2026-11-10. For 26 November it shows RTVE's four-way as "proposal, not confirmed" and the laSexta Xplica "Mesa Abierta" spokespeople panel, which would not count. [Politicheck](https://politicheck.es/29n-debates)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Several outlets report the 26 November date, citing negotiating-team sources via EFE. The Academia has not issued a formal statement, and I found no announced time or confirmed list of participants.
- 2026-11-15: Vozpópuli says the date, organiser (the Academia) and broadcaster (RTVE) are set. It names Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau as planned participants, but calls the format "previsto" (planned). [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/politica/el-calendario-de-los-debates-electorales-ya-esta-cerrado-estas-son-las-citas-claves-antes-del-29-n.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: El Plural (citing EFE) says the four-way will be on the 26th, organised by the Academia, which will offer an institutional signal that any channel can carry. The four leaders are expected. The Academia has asked the Junta Electoral Central (JEC) whether Irene Montero (Podemos) can take part, which would make it a five-way. [El Plural](https://www.elplural.com/extratele/debate-cuatro-sera-26-noviembre-podemos-queda-pendiente-junta-electoral_804221102)
- 2026-11-15: Vozpópuli reports that the PSOE says it is not vetoing Podemos, but that if the debate is widened, Alvise Pérez should also be invited. [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/politica/el-calendario-de-los-debates-electorales-ya-esta-cerrado-estas-son-las-citas-claves-antes-del-29-n.html)
- 2026-11-14: EFE, via Infobae and regional papers, reports that the debate of the main candidates will be on the 26th, one week after the cara a cara. It will keep the cara a cara's five thematic blocks. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2026/11/14/el-debate-de-los-principales-candidatos-sera-el-dia-26-una-semana-despues-del-cara-a-cara/); [Tribuna de Segovia](https://www.tribunasegovia.com/noticias/466568/sanchez-feijoo-abascal-y-colau-debatiran-el-dia-26-a-la-espera-de-que-la-junta-electoral-decida-sobre-podemos)
- 2026-11-14: RTVE's own schedule article confirms only the 19 November cara a cara and the 23 November eight-way debate. [RTVE](https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20261114/debates-electorales-29-n-11-n-horario-donde-ver-tv/17314377.shtml)
- 2026-11-13: The Academia confirms the Sánchez-Feijóo cara a cara for 19 November at 22:00, moderated by María Casado. [El Español](https://www.elespanol.com/espana/politica/20261113/cara-sanchez-feijoo-celebrara-noviembre-organizado-academia-television/1003744457727_0.html)
- 2026-11-12: Podemos accuses the PSOE and Frente Amplio of trying to exclude it from the Academia debate. [Teleprensa](https://www.teleprensa.com/nacional-3/podemos-acusa-psoe-frente-amplio-tratar-expularles-debate-electoral-que-organiza-academia-tv/202611121252522555742.html)
- 2026-11-10: Montero says Podemos will be in the Academia debate. Format and speaking times were unresolved. [ElConstitucional](https://www.elconstitucional.es/en/national/politics/podemos-announces-it-will-be-in-the-electoral-debate-of-the-television-academy-and-opens-negotiations-with-the-broad-front-over-the-times_9994_102.html)
- As of 2026-11-16, I found no JEC ruling.

## 4. Base rates
- July 2023: The only multi-leader debate (RTVE, 19 July) had Sánchez, Díaz and Abascal. Feijóo did not attend, but three leaders were still there. [Doble Lectura](https://doblelectura.es/guia/debates-electorales-elecciones-generales-2026)
- November 2019: The Academia/RTVE five-way went ahead with all main leaders, on the Monday of the campaign's second week (my recollection, not checked here).
- April 2019: The RTVE four-way and the Atresmedia four-way were held on consecutive days after a dispute over dates, so dates moved late.
- December 2015: Atresmedia's four-way ran with Sáenz de Santamaría standing in for Rajoy, which still meant three leaders were present.
- Pattern: once the major parties have agreed to a multi-candidate debate in Spain, it has usually happened with at least three leaders. Dates have sometimes shifted by a day or more.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on whether this debate happens.
- Related markets (2026-11-16): Polymarket gives PP 80.5% and PSOE 19.5% to win the election. Kalshi gives Feijóo 85% to become PM. These are not directly relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The JEC ruling on whether Podemos can join (expected any day). This could turn the debate into a five-way, or lead to friction that delays or derails it, for example over the PSOE's demand to include Alvise.
- The Academia's formal announcement of the date, time and participants for the 26th.
- 19 November: the Sánchez-Feijóo cara a cara. How it goes could change the parties' incentives to attend the 26th.
- 23 November: RTVE's spokespeople debate, and possibly Atresmedia's four-way. If Atresmedia's goes ahead, a leader might skip the 26th.
- Risk to watch: the date slipping to the 25th or 27th (the 19 November cara a cara already slipped from the 16th). The campaign ends at 24:00 on 27 November.

None of them gives a start time, and I found no official statement from the Academia, RTVE or the parties.

## 1. Resolution source

Its status reads: planned, according to Vozpópuli, with the Academia and RTVE, but "Sin confirmación de la Academia ni de los partidos, ni hora; Podemos pide estar" (no confirmation from the Academia or the parties, no time; Podemos wants to take part). It has also seen no Junta Electoral Central (JEC) decision on debates. [Doble Lectura](https://doblelectura.es/guia/debates-electorales-elecciones-generales-2026)
- The same tracker still lists Atresmedia's four-way for Monday 23 November as uncertain. Feijóo and Abascal said yes, Frente Amplio backed out and Sánchez has not accepted. [Doble Lectura](https://doblelectura.es/guia/debates-electorales-elecciones-generales-2026)
- Politicheck was last updated on 10 November and is out of date. For 26 November it shows laSexta's spokespeople panel "Mesa Abierta" (announced) and RTVE's proposed four-way (not confirmed). [Politicheck](https://politicheck.es/29n-debates)
- The Academia's own page mentions only the Sánchez-Feijóo cara a cara on 19 November. It says nothing about a 26 November debate. [AcademiaTV](https://www.academiatv.es/la-academia-de-television-punto-de-encuentro-para-los-debates-electorales-2026)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. The 26 November four-way is widely reported but not formally announced, and no time is given.
- The open issue is whether Podemos takes part, which could make it a five-way. That would not affect resolution as long as at least three of the four named leaders attend.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

## 4. Base rates
Past general elections where a debate included at least three of the main national leaders:
- December 2015: Atresmedia four-way. Rajoy was replaced by Sáenz de Santamaría, but Sánchez, Iglesias and Rivera attended, so three leaders.
- June 2016: Academia four-way with all four leaders.
- April 2019: two four-ways with leaders, on RTVE (22 April) and Atresmedia (23 April).
- November 2019: Academia five-way with all leaders (4 November).
- July 2023: RTVE three-way with Sánchez, Díaz and Abascal. Feijóo did not attend.

So every general election since 2015 had at least one debate with three or more top leaders, usually in the final campaign week. The main risk for this question is the date: such debates have been moved at short notice, including the cara a cara this year, which went from 16 to 19 November.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on whether this debate happens.
- Related markets (as of 2026-11-16) do not bear directly on this question: Polymarket has PP winning at 0.805 and PSOE at 0.195, and Kalshi has Feijóo as the next prime minister at 0.85.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- An official announcement from the Academia or RTVE of the 26 November four-way, with a start time.
- The JEC ruling on Podemos, plus the PSOE's demand to include Alvise. A dispute here could delay the debate, change its format or cause a boycott.
- The cara a cara on 19 November. How it goes could change whether candidates want to attend the four-way. For example, the frontrunner Feijóo might skip it, as Rajoy did in 2015 and Feijóo did in 2023. Even then, three of the four could still attend.
- Whether the Atresmedia four-way on 23 November takes place, which could draw candidates away from the 26th.
- laSexta's spokespeople panel on 26 November does not count towards this question.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10.5 days remain; the outcome is known on the evening of 26 November 2026. For Yes, a debate must start on 26 November (CET) on a nationwide Spanish channel, with at least three of Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau debating together in person in the same studio.

(b) Status quo: since 14 November, EFE (citing negotiating-team sources), Vozpópuli and El Plural have reported an Academia-organised four-way on Thursday 26 November, with all four leaders expected. If nothing changes, this resolves Yes. However, no formal announcement or start time exists yet. The Doble Lectura tracker (15 November) marks it "sin confirmación".

(c) Base rate: every Spanish general election since 2015 has had at least one debate with three or more top leaders, so roughly 5 of 5. For a specific pre-reported date holding, the reference class is weaker. Dates shifted in April 2019, and this campaign's cara a cara slipped from the 16th to the 19th. I estimate a reported but unconfirmed debate date holds about 75-80% of the time.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- EFE (14 November) and El Plural (15 November) report the date, organiser, institutional signal and the five thematic blocks.
- The PP itself asked for the 26th, which lowers the risk that Feijóo pulls out.
- The PSOE linked the cara a cara to a four-way.
- Only three of the four leaders are needed.

Evidence for No:
- No Academia statement or start time exists as of 15-16 November.
- The JEC ruling on Podemos is pending, and the PSOE wants Alvise included if Podemos is, so a format dispute could delay the debate.
- The Atresmedia four-way on 23 November could compete for leaders.
- The cara a cara date already slipped once.

(e) No scenario: the JEC orders Podemos included, the PSOE demands Alvise, and negotiations drag on. The debate moves to Wednesday 25 November or collapses, leaving only laSexta's spokespeople panel on the 26th.

Yes scenario: the Academia formally announces a 22:00 debate on the 26th after the JEC ruling. Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau (possibly with Montero) debate, carried on RTVE and other channels.

(f) I start at about 78% given the strong, consistent reporting. I trim slightly for the lack of formal confirmation and the pending Podemos and Alvise dispute that could shift the date. The three-of-four threshold buffers against a single boycott.

Probability: 76%

(b) Status quo: EFE (citing negotiating-team sources), Vozpópuli and El Plural all report an Academia four-way on 26 November with all four leaders. If those plans hold, the question resolves YES. It is not formally confirmed, though: there is no time, no Academia statement, and RTVE's 14 November schedule does not list it.

(c) Base rate: In every Spanish general election since 2015, at least one debate included three or more top leaders (5 out of 5). Once major parties have agreed to a multi-candidate debate, it has nearly always gone ahead. Dates have shifted, however, as in April 2019 and with this year's cara a cara, which moved from 16 to 19 November. For "it happens on a specific reported date," I would put the base rate around 70-80%.

(d) Evidence for YES:
- On 14 November, EFE reported the 26 November date with Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau, keeping the cara a cara's five blocks.
